title: Batch 3 Exodus–Judges Curation Methodology
notes: Batch 3 separates textual sequence, site identification, archaeological chronology, later tradition, and route reconstruction. Unknown stations are not given synthetic coordinates; candidate sites are visibly labeled.
verificationNote: Project-authored curation methodology; no external source verification claim is implied.

title: The Oxford History of the Biblical World
author: Michael D. Coogan, ed.
notes: Broad academic orientation for Late Bronze/Iron Age historical context and the emergence of Israel. Page-level citations remain an editorial follow-up before an academic-grade release.

title: Israel in Egypt: The Evidence for the Authenticity of the Exodus Tradition
author: James K. Hoffmeier
notes: Used as one scholarly treatment of Egyptian geography and Exodus traditions; not treated as a sole or consensus authority.

title: Ancient Israel in Sinai: The Evidence for the Authenticity of the Wilderness Tradition
author: James K. Hoffmeier
notes: Used for Sinai-route and wilderness-geography orientation alongside other atlases; proposals remain labeled by confidence.

title: Who Were the Early Israelites and Where Did They Come From?
author: William G. Dever
notes: Academic archaeological synthesis used for early Israel/highland-settlement context. Specific interpretive claims are not presented as unanimous consensus.

title: The Archaeology of the Israelite Settlement
author: Israel Finkelstein
notes: Foundational survey-based study of Iron I highland settlement used as context for the Judges-era transition. Later scholarship has refined and debated parts of its interpretation.

title: Digging Up Jericho
author: Kathleen M. Kenyon
notes: Classic excavation synthesis relevant to Jericho chronology. Later reassessments exist; the atlas explicitly marks the Joshua correlation as disputed.

title: The Archaeology of Ancient Israel
author: Amnon Ben-Tor, ed.
notes: General archaeological reference for Canaanite and early Israelite sites; used for orientation rather than fabricated pinpoint citations.

title: The Archaeology of Jordan
author: Burton MacDonald, Russell Adams, and Piotr Bienkowski, eds.
notes: Regional archaeological orientation for Moab, Edom, Ammon, and Transjordan. Exact page-level citations remain editorial work.
